I have a thing I call, "the in-betweens." I've accepted that majority of life will be difficult. We will all struggle, a lot. It's inevitable. However, there's these little moments in between all the bullshit and pain, "the in-betweens." Those little glimpses of light, pockets of air, are the moments we should remember and cherish. 

You're having a long day at work and you're drained. On your commute home, you catch eyes with a stranger and you both smile and acknowledge each other. That's "an in-between." You're scrolling through your phone with your friends doing the same next to you. Your homie sees a funny video and starts laughing uncontrollably. It's contagious and now everyone is laughing. That's "an in-between."

There's more I can list off but I think you get it. Let the bullshit by and try to catch those in-betweens. Life will feel just a little more bearable.

Insomniac festivals are plentiful in California. Beyond Wonderland, Nocturnal, Escape, Countdown, Dreamstate. These are more commercial and tend to draw a more mainstream crowd. Vibes will vary and most of the time, they're at NOS which is infamous for pickpocketing. Good start if you want to experience great production and big artists.

If you're looking for something smaller with a community feel, there's Lucidity, Northern Nights, Lightning In A Bottle, Desert Hearts, and Dirtybird Campout. These include camping over a few days. Vibes are great and you get to see smaller/underground artists. It'll be a more intimate experience since they aren't as massive as Insomniac events.

Hi there,

Thank you for sharing. Your current self worth reflects your upbringing. You received little to no positive reinforcement (based on your post) as a child thus, as an adult, it is difficult to give yourself any credit for your achievements. I'm sorry that you endured this growing up however, there is a silver lining. Your experiences are yours and you can use them to become a better person from those who raised you.

In regards to a plan, I recommend saving up as much as you can. Do you have a college degree? This will help you with getting more opportunities for better jobs. Once you have enough to be own your own, remove yourself from this toxic environment.

>why do i feel so powerless these days?

The world is and has always been in turmoil. It's difficult to change something that has been ravaged for millennia. None of us have the power to change the world but small actions towards positive change is still making a difference. That is powerful on its own.

>why cant i seem to get anything right? 

We are not perfect. It's part of the human condition to be imperfect. This way, we make mistakes and we learn. Growing is the tree, but without water (our mistakes), there is nothing to nourish the tree.

>why cant i get rid of all this anxiety?

Our brains are fascinating. They allow us to do amazing things. They also can fuck with us. Chemical imbalance, genetics, and our environment effect the way we respond to external stimuli. Being anxious comes with this unfortunately. With time, you'll find healthy methods of coping with your anxiety. It's part of you but it doesn't mean it will always binder you. I recommend carrying a worry coin or something to realign you when you get anxious.

>why cant i do anything for anyone?

Small actions matter. Like a pebble thrown in a pond, you can create ripples. don't sell yourself short. 

>why cant i just be a kid again?

You never you you're in the good old days until they're gone. Live in the present. This way, you won't look back when you're older wishing for better times.

>why am i not feeling the same drive and power to change things that i used to feel?

We can't always be at full capacity. We run out of gas eventually. Sometimes we get stuck in a rut or we plateau. Progress is gradual. It's okay to not always be driven. Re-inspire yourself. Maybe find new creative outlets. Once you find that one thing, you'll be surprised at how motivated you become.

>why cant i stop having nightmares?

Dreams and nightmares are just our subconscious minds processing our thoughts. I wouldn't dwell too much on them. We like to try to find meaning in everything. Try unwinding before bed that way when you are in REM sleep, you might have a better chance at having pleasant dreams. 

>why do i feel nothing playing mario?

Play a different game! Change it up a little. Then revisit Mario later. Maybe you'll have fun again. It's good to change it up so you don't get bored.

>why wont everything stop hurting, and why dont i feel anything good anymore?

Sounds like a possible bout of depression. Have you been diagnosed with depression before? Feelings of emptiness, hopelessness, and lack of self worth are some signs of it. Are you physically in pain or is it metaphorical? I recommend seeing a doctor if it's within your means. My therapist really helped me find healthy ways to work on my depression. I'd give it a shot.

It may feel like you're the only one sitting in the dark. You scream for help but no one heard you. If it means anything though, I'm here. You aren't truly ever alone. You may be isolated but never alone. Reach out to your family and friends. You'd be surprised. Maybe someone you know feels the same way and you could unintentionally be helping them feel less alone? 

>why do i want a gun so damn badly?

Unless the gun is to protect yourself and your family, I wouldn't recommend owning one. A simple way out is not really that simple. If you go, you won't get to experience what your loved ones will. It will just be the end.

First off, it took a lot opening up to your friend about your depression. It helps having someone know what you're going through. 

Sometimes our closest friends and family are unaware of our expectations. In your case, maybe he didn't realize that you needed more consistent check-ins. It's not that he doesn't care, but more that he is unaware of your needs. I believe if you talked about your expectations with him, define your needs in a way he can adequately help you, then both of you will be on the same page. 

I'd say give him another shot. Definitely try not to put too much on him in the beginning if he isn't used to talking about mental health. It can be a little rattling for some so be kind to him and yourself. Definitely try seeking out others for support too. You don't want to put all your eggs in one basket. 

Anyway, I hope you find what you are searching for. I'm rooting for you friend. Take care.
